children: Venture capital firm Accel India and 360 ONE Group sold a little over 4 per cent stake in omnichannel jewellery retailer BlueStone for ₹513 crore through separate block deals on the BSE.
The two investors sold a combined 61.98 lakh shares on Thursday, representing a 4.07 per cent stake in Bengaluru-based BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle, according to exchange data.

Accel India, through its affiliate Accel India III (Mauritius) Ltd, sold 28 lakh shares, or a 1.84 per cent stake, while 360 ONE Group, through its funds, offloaded 33.98 lakh shares or a 2.23 per cent stake in the jewellery retailer.
The transactions were executed at an average price of ₹827.60 per share, taking the deal value to ₹513 crore.
With the latest transaction, Accel's holding through its affiliates declined to 8.71 per cent from 10.55 per cent.
The shares, however, found buyers among a mix of domestic and overseas institutional investors, who acquired an equal number of shares at the same price.
Mutual Funds managed by Mirae Asset, Nippon India, and Bandhan, along with Bajaj Life Insurance, participated in the transaction.
In addition, SBI Life Insurance also bought over 9.5 lakh shares, or a 0.6 per cent stake for ₹79 crore, raising its stake in the jewellery retailer to 5.02 per cent from 4.4 per cent.
Goldman Sachs, Citigroup Global Markets Singapore and sovereign wealth fund Kuwait Investment Authority were among the foreign investors participating in the transaction.
The stock of BlueStone Jewellery and Lifestyle on Friday fell 1.48 per cent to trade at ₹793.10 per share on the BSE.
The stake sale follows a stronger first-quarter performance by BlueStone.
In July, the company reported a consolidated net profit of ₹5.96 crore for the April-June quarter, compared with a net loss of ₹34.74 crore a year ago.
Its total income rose 49 per cent to ₹751.81 crore, while expenses increased to ₹744.82 crore from ₹538.45 crore.
The latest selloff marks the second round of stake sales by the investors this year.
In June, Accel, 360 ONE and IvyCap Ventures had sold shares of BlueStone for nearly ₹243 crore.

Founded in 2011 by Gaurav Singh Kushwaha and Vidya Nataraj, BlueStone offers more than 8,000 designs across rings, pendants, earrings and competes with Titan's CaratLane, GIVA and other jewellery brands.

title: Accel India, 360 ONE Group sell over 4% stake in BlueStone for ₹513 cr
